source_caption:
"This movie is set 10 minutes from now", Alex Garland famously said in his 2014 directorial debut, Ex Machina. 

And looking at the current state of AI, that clock is ticking. This isn't just a sci-fi monologue; it’s a eulogy for the human race. Garland used this phrase to describe the film's near-future setting, meaning that the advanced artificial intelligence technology portrayed in the movie is close enough to reality that if a major tech company like Google or Apple announced it tomorrow, it would be surprising, but not completely unbelievable. What's your thoughts on this?!

source_details.title: Ex Machina
source_details.synopsis: Ex Machina is a 2014 science fiction film, written and directed by Alex Garland in his directorial debut. It stars Domhnall Gleeson, Alicia Vikander, and Oscar Isaac. It follows a programmer who is invited by his CEO to administer the Turing test to an intelligent female humanoid robot. Ex Machina premiered at the BFI Southbank on 16 December 2014. It was released in the United Kingdom on 21 January 2015, by Universal Pictures International, and in the United States on 10 April 2015, by A24. It grossed over $36.8 million worldwide on a $15 million budget. Ex Machina received acclaim for its visual effects, screenplay and performances.
